Stage 3 of 5 · Find your people

Find Your People

The physical part is mostly over. Now comes the stretch where most people go back, and the single biggest difference between those who do and those who don't is other people.

You're here if

  • You've got a week or more behind you
  • The evenings are long and the cravings arrive out of nowhere
  • You know you should "get support" and have no idea what that looks like
  • The idea of a church hall full of sixty-year-olds makes you want to drink

The job of this stage

Find at least one room, one person and one way through a craving. I got sober in AA and I'll always credit it. But I also know how daunting those rooms can be when everyone in them has decades on you. So this stage covers the rooms and everything beyond them. The research is clear that connection is the thing. Which kind is up to you.

Read these, in this order

  1. MeetingsFree, everywhere, and the evidence is strong. Also: why they feel daunting at 20.→
  2. Your First MeetingWhat actually happens, what you have to say (nothing), what it costs (nothing).→
  3. Beyond the rooms: other optionsSMART, Dharma, LifeRing, counselling, medication. The rest of the menu.→
  4. CravingsA craving is a wave. It peaks and passes, whether you drink or not.→
  5. Build your support networkThe six kinds of support, and how to find your first person.→

Shortcut

Not sure which kind of support suits you? Find Your Room is a six-question quiz that sorts it out in a minute.
